text:
Looking at the climate results for the 2050s under middle-of-the-road emissions, the best match for the farm's future climate is Whitman County, WA. This is a strong match, and all 8 climate models agree on it. 

To understand how close these climate matches are, the results use sigma: lower means the place's climate today is closer to the farm's future climate. 

Regarding rotations, the field's current rotation is used in 1 of the matching areas. The rotations used at the matching places include a flexible mix of fallow, spring wheat, and winter wheat; winter wheat to fallow; and winter wheat to spring wheat to fallow. 

Comparing hazards at the best match, Whitman County, WA experiences 28 days above 32c per year today compared to 18 on the field today. It has 186 frost-free days compared to 150 on the field today. For the driest-month soil water percentage in September, it is 17.2 percent at the match compared to 16.6 percent on the field today.

Across the year, temperatures are projected to increase while precipitation changes vary. Keep in mind that these candidates are based on 3351 farmland cells at approximately 4 kilometers using the Cropland Data Layer.
